page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 12 vCPUs distributed across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2.

The hardware configuration provides 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for operational disk persistence. Hardware acceleration is absent, with no GPUs available. Networking capability is configured with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and the instance comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes show average multi-threaded execution balanced against weak single-threaded performance. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 4693.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 10161.81, whereas the single-core Geekbench score measured at 930.0 and single-threaded gzip compression registered in the lowest percentiles. Memory performance delivered 59.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 49.35 GB/sec for uncached writes, yielding a PassMark database operations metric of 3243.33 and Redis SET performance of 8.48 million operations per second. Language model evaluation exhibits modest small-model prompt handling at 668.6 tokens per second, but throughput drops to 7.48 tokens per second during medium-model text generation.

The ecs.se1ne.3xlarge delivers balanced resource density specifically oriented toward memory-intensive operations. While single-thread instruction throughput and network bandwidth are constrained, the high memory allocation makes the instance practical for in-memory caching systems, Redis databases, medium-scale relational databases, and batch data processing workloads that rely primarily on RAM capacity.
